findings.text: All three guards proven non-tautological by mutation: removing the empty-interactions guard, or reverting check_invariant / check_budget to their is-not-None form, each turns exactly one named selftest case red (integration empty-interactions; db missing-expect_rows; db missing-max_seconds), 762/1 in each case.

Guards use is None (not truthiness) so expect_rows:[] and max_seconds:0.0 remain legitimate strict assertions; real row mismatches, SQL errors, and budget overruns are still caught. The pre-existing SQL-error selftest was given an expect_rows so it still exercises the real SQL path rather than tripping the new guard - an honest adjustment, not a weakening.

Fixtures unaffected: db pass/fail and integration pass/fail behave as before (db fail still fails at reversibility, empty budgets:[] legitimate, a no-invariants-no-budgets journey still passes). Web runner exclusion is honest (Node .mjs, not exercised in the gate).

summary: WARP-0411 closes three silent-pass gaps in two mechanical runners: the integration runner now fails loud on empty/missing interactions, and the db runner's check_invariant and check_budget fail loud with named malformed errors when their assertion is under-declared. Independent adversarial review: pass_with_notes, 0 blocking, gate GREEN (763/0). Each guard is genuinely non-tautological (mutation flips its dedicated selftest case), well-formed checks still pass, and real mismatches/SQL errors/budget overruns are still caught. Proportionate, generic, ASCII, no protected path.
